h1: The Plimplace Hotel — Saltwater Pool, Spacious Rooms, 5-Min BTS Walk in Lat Phrao
intro: Positioned right beside Bangkok's iconic Elephant Building on Phahonyothin Road, The Plimplace Hotel is a 3-star property that punches above its price tag with spacious rooms starting at 35 sqm, a genuine outdoor saltwater pool, and a 5-minute stroll to BTS Phahon Yothin 24 — putting Central Ladprao, Chatuchak Weekend Market and Mo Chit well within easy reach. Rooms from approx. ฿1,000/night · Score 8.7 from 367 reviews on Trip.com.

body.html: The address — 3338 Phahonyothin Road — says everything about this hotel's location. The property sits directly next to the Elephant Building, one of Bangkok's most recognisable landmarks, in the Ha Yaek Lat Phrao intersection district. Walk out the door and in five minutes you're at BTS Phahon Yothin 24 (Exit 4), where you can ride one stop to Central Ladprao shopping mall or continue onward to connect with the MRT at Phahon Yothin station. For anyone who wants to explore Bangkok without depending on taxis, this interchange location is hard to beat at this price.

The most consistent praise across guest reviews is the room size. Deluxe Rooms start at 35–37 sqm, each with a private balcony, refrigerator, flat-screen TV and free Wi-Fi — considerably more space than similarly priced hotels in this district. The 40-sqm Super Deluxe fits three single beds, making it a practical choice for groups. The One Bedroom Suite (46–51 sqm) offers a fully separate living area that feels closer to a serviced apartment than a standard hotel room, while the Two Bedroom Suite at 66 sqm comfortably handles families.
"Huge room, spotlessly clean, great location — five-minute walk to BTS. Easily the best value I found in Bangkok for the price."

The outdoor saltwater pool on the 2nd floor is open daily from 07:00 to 21:00 and is genuinely well-maintained. Among 3-star hotels in this price bracket, finding an actual usable pool is rare — and here guests consistently call it clean and peaceful, especially in the early morning before the sun gets intense. The fitness centre shares the same floor. There's also a coin laundry in the building (30–40 baht per load), which long-stay guests particularly appreciate. The in-house Prim Sabai Cafe serves breakfast and lunch, though it's open Monday to Saturday only.

Honesty first: the hotel has real weaknesses that appear consistently across Booking.com and Trip.com reviews. Sound insulation is poor. Multiple guests mention hearing everything from adjacent rooms and the corridor — doors slamming, conversations, early-morning departures. A ฿1,000 cash deposit (roughly $28) is required at check-in; this surprises guests who haven't read the fine print. There are also a handful of reviews citing inflexibility around late check-out. And breakfast, when available, is described as basic rather than impressive.

What keeps the overall score at 8.7 is the ratio of space, location and price. Free parking with EV charging is an added bonus for guests driving in. A 7-Eleven is essentially attached to the property, Lotus's supermarket is a short walk away, and Union Mall is about 10 minutes on foot. For travellers who plan to spend most of their time out exploring — Chatuchak Market, Or Tor Kor fresh market, Ratchayothin area, or commuting across the city — the Plimplace makes a solid, affordable base.

Overall, The Plimplace Hotel delivers what its score promises: a clean, spacious, well-located room at a fair price with a real pool. It isn't trying to be a boutique property with memorable service touches — and that's fine. If you're a light sleeper or want polished hospitality, look elsewhere. If you want value, room to breathe and easy BTS access in a neighbourhood that actually has things to do, this is a solid choice.

highlights.title: 5-Min Walk to BTS
highlights.text: Step out the door and reach BTS Phahon Yothin 24 in 5 minutes — one stop to Central Ladprao, two stops to Chatuchak, easy MRT interchange at Phahon Yothin.

highlights.title: Outdoor Saltwater Pool
highlights.text: Open 07:00–21:00 daily on the 2nd floor. Clean, well-maintained and rarely crowded in the early morning — genuinely unusual at this price and star level.

highlights.title: Rooms Larger Than the Price Suggests
highlights.text: Deluxe rooms from 35 sqm with private balcony; suites up to 66 sqm with separate living area. More space per baht than most competitors in the area.

honestSummary: The Plimplace Hotel genuinely delivers on the three things that matter most at this price: large rooms, a real pool and a walkable BTS connection. Just go in knowing the sound insulation is poor, the deposit is cash only, and check-out is firm at noon.
honestChecks: If you're a light sleeper — multiple reviews confirm walls are paper-thin and corridor noise carries clearly, especially at night when other guests come and go → bring earplugs or request a higher floor facing away from the lift

If you want a quality breakfast — Prim Sabai Cafe is basic and only open Mon–Sat; it doesn't compare to hotel breakfast at a higher tier → plan to walk outside; great local food options surround the hotel
If you need a late check-out — the hotel enforces noon strictly and a few guests had unpleasant experiences around this → agree terms in advance at check-in and don't leave it to the morning rush

tips.title: Swim early for a quiet pool
tips.body: The saltwater pool opens at 07:00. Hit it in the first hour and you'll often have it to yourself — water's freshest and the morning light is beautiful before the heat sets in.

tips.title: Use BTS Exit 4 from Phahon Yothin 24
tips.body: Take Exit 4 from BTS Phahon Yothin 24 and walk toward the Elephant Building. The hotel entrance is right next to it — no need to cross any major roads.

tips.title: Bring ฿1,000 cash for the deposit
tips.body: The hotel requires a ฿1,000 cash damage deposit on arrival. It's returned at check-out. Have it ready to avoid hunting for an ATM after a long journey.

tips.title: Chatuchak Weekend Market is two BTS stops away
tips.body: From BTS Phahon Yothin 24, ride two stops north to Mo Chit for Chatuchak. Go before 10:00 on Saturday or Sunday — the market fills up fast and the best stalls thin out by midday.

faq.q: Where is The Plimplace Hotel and can I walk to the BTS?
faq.a: The hotel is at 3338 Phahonyothin Road, next to the Elephant Building in the Ha Yaek Lat Phrao district, Chatuchak. It's a 5-minute walk to BTS Phahon Yothin 24 (Exit 4) — one stop to Central Ladprao, two to Chatuchak, with easy MRT interchange at Phahon Yothin station. Don Mueang Airport is around 20 minutes by car.

faq.q: What rooms does The Plimplace Hotel have and what do they cost?
faq.a: Rooms start from approx. ฿1,000/night for a Deluxe Room (35–37 sqm, private balcony). Super Deluxe (3 single beds, 40 sqm) from ~฿1,300. One Bedroom Suite (46–51 sqm, separate living room) from ~฿1,700. Two Bedroom Suite (66 sqm) from ~฿2,200. Prices vary by platform and season — compare before booking.

faq.q: Does The Plimplace Hotel have a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes — an outdoor saltwater swimming pool on the 2nd floor, open 07:00–21:00 daily. Guests consistently describe it as clean and well-maintained. A fitness centre is located on the same floor.

faq.q: Is The Plimplace Hotel good for families?
faq.a: Reasonably yes. The Two Bedroom Suite (66 sqm) handles families of 3–4 comfortably. Free parking is a bonus for families driving in. The main caution is noise — thin walls mean children's noise (and others') carries, so request a high floor if you have young kids who nap.

faq.q: What are the most common complaints about The Plimplace Hotel?
faq.a: The most consistent complaints across Booking.com and Trip.com are: poor sound insulation (thin walls, audible corridor noise), a ฿1,000 cash-only deposit required at check-in, and rigid late check-out policy. Breakfast is also described as basic rather than impressive. None of these are dealbreakers if you know in advance.
